claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution with homogeneously distributed elements.
Service-like thermal exposure causes diffusion-mediated phase separation of the metastable solid solution.
The transformation nucleates intermetallic precipitates both within grains and along grain boundaries.
Mg-containing multi-principal-element alloys can contain Mg-rich phases and intermetallic compounds such as Mg-Zn and Ti-Zn phases.
Intermetallic precipitates produced under moderate exposure remain fine and uniformly dispersed.
The fine intermetallic precipitates are coherent with the surrounding matrix.
Fine intermetallic precipitates act as nucleation sites for a continuous, adherent protective oxide layer.
Formation of a protective oxide layer can enhance passivation and lower corrosion current density in an Mg-containing alloy.
The fine-precipitate-supported oxide layer retains or improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Higher-temperature or longer thermal exposure causes intermetallic precipitates to grow and coarsen.
Aggressive thermal exposure causes intermetallic phases to segregate or become unevenly distributed.
Coarsened or segregated intermetallic phases disrupt the continuity of the protective oxide scale.
Loss of oxide-scale continuity increases corrosion susceptibility.
Loss of oxide-scale continuity degrades high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Annealing at approximately 600–750°C for short durations should produce fine precipitates, a continuous oxide, and corrosion and oxidation performance superior to the as-processed state.

Annealing above 900°C or for prolonged durations should produce coarse intermetallics, a discontinuous or non-protective oxide, and poorer corrosion and oxidation performance than the as-processed state.
The transition from fine to coarse intermetallic distributions marks the service boundary between retained and lost corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The precise time-temperature thresholds and compositional dependence of the proposed transformation remain undetermined.
